summary: Specifies the sms Uniform Resource Identifier scheme, which names one or more recipients for an SMS text message. A link using it can start composing a message on a mobile phone or equipped device. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Just like a web link opens a page, a link of this kind opens a new text message ready to send to a chosen phone number.

questions: what is the sms uri scheme
how to make a link that opens a text message
how to write an sms link with a message body
how to send an sms to multiple recipients in a uri
is the sms uri scheme secure
subtitle: A link format that opens a text message addressed to one or more phone numbers.

tldr.problem: Web pages and documents could link to email addresses with mailto, but had no standard way to link to a phone number for sending an SMS text message.
tldr.mechanism: The sms URI scheme lists one or more telephone numbers, separated by commas, and may carry a body field with the initial message text, as in sms:+15105550101?body=hello%20there.
tldr.outcome: User agents can start message composition when a user selects such a link, and IANA registered the scheme as Permanent. Sending must not happen without the user's confirmation.

today: RFC 5724 is a Proposed Standard from January 2010. The metadata for this RFC lists no obsoleting or updating documents.

sections.title: SMS and Why It Needs a URI
sections.content:
The Short Message Service (SMS) is an integral part of GSM mobile networks. SMS messages are alphanumeric paging messages with a maximum length of 160 characters (7-bit characters) or 140 octets. UCS-2 characters, giving 70-character messages, MAY also be supported. Longer text is possible by concatenation, and clients composing messages SHOULD use the standard concatenation method from the SMS specification.

The mailto scheme is popular because user agents offer an email composition facility when a user selects it. The sms scheme aims at the same thing for text messages: user agents such as Web browsers and email clients can offer SMS composition when the URI is selected, or open a Web page that provides it.

Messages are stored by an SMS Center (SMSC) for delivery. The scheme cannot name an SMSC, so if a specific one is needed, some other context must establish it.
sections.eli5: Email links already open a new email. This memo wants a link that opens a new text message in the same way.

sections.title: The sms URI Syntax
sections.content:
An sms URI is the scheme sms, a colon, a comma-separated list of recipients, and optional fields after a question mark. Each recipient is a telephone-subscriber as defined in RFC 3966, which means a global number starting with + unless it cannot be written that way. Keywords are case-insensitive.

Fields are joined with &. This RFC defines a single field, body, which MUST NOT appear more than once. It holds percent-encoded UTF-8 text that implementations MUST convert to a suitable SMS character encoding. If characters are discarded or converted, the user MUST be notified. Unknown fields MUST be ignored, and extensions MAY define more fields but MUST NOT change the meaning of this specification.

User agents SHOULD support multiple recipients and SHOULD make the full recipient list clear before committing to sending.
sections.eli5: The link says who to text, and can also say what the first words of the text should be. Anything the program does not understand, it ignores.

sections.title: Processing and Comparing sms URIs
sections.content:
To process a URI, the user agent extracts the first recipient's number, which MUST be in international form with country code unless it only works inside a certain area or network. It then extracts the body field if present. It SHOULD offer a way to compose the message, starting from the body text, and then SHOULD try its default delivery method first, with MAY-level fallback to another method.

With several recipients, exactly the same message SHOULD go to all of them. Simply activating a link SHOULD NOT send a message without prior user confirmation. Messages sent because of such a URI MUST be sent as class 1 SMS messages if the user agent can set the message class.

Two sms URIs are equivalent when their fields are identical and their recipients, compared as a set without regard to order, are equivalent under the RFC 3966 rules. Those rules ignore visual separators, and comparison is case-insensitive.
sections.eli5: The program takes the number, fills in the starting text, lets you edit it, and only sends when you say so. Every person on the list gets the same message.

sections.title: Examples and HTML Forms
sections.content:
The RFC gives three examples: sms:+15105550101 for one recipient, sms:+15105550101,+15105550102 for two, and sms:+15105550101?body=hello%20there for a message that starts as "hello there" and may be edited before sending.

An sms URI can also be the action of an HTML form. The form data is packaged as with mailto, using application/x-www-form-urlencoded, as UTF-8 text with no HTTP header fields. The URI's own body field is ignored in this case. If the submission is too long for one SMS, the user agent MAY concatenate messages or refuse to send, but it MUST NOT send partial form submissions.
sections.eli5: A web form can also send its answers as a text message. If the answers do not fit in one text, the program either sends several linked texts or sends nothing at all.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
SMS messages travel without any provisions for privacy or integrity, and there is no framework for layering security on top. Delivery time is not guaranteed: messages between operators sometimes take hours or even days, or never arrive, so applications SHOULD NOT assume anything about reliability.

Sending SMS usually costs money, so clients MUST make sure any action that incurs costs is acknowledged by the end user, and the user MUST be able to control which submission route is used. Special SMS messages exist that can, for example, turn on display indicators or send data to ports on the device, so clients and gateways SHOULD filter such User Data header fields. Unchecked user input MUST NOT populate any field other than the User Data field.

Spreading sms URIs in unsolicited messages could be used to reveal a person's phone number or link it to an email identity. User agents MAY also let users filter numbers in local format, since most premium-rate numbers use it.
sections.eli5: Texts are like postcards that anyone could read, they can arrive late, and sending them can cost money. So a program should always ask you before it sends one.

sections.title: Scheme Registration
sections.content: The memo requests registration of the sms URI scheme under the guidelines of RFC 4395, with status Permanent. The registration says the scheme works in a similar way to mailto, that no interoperability issues have been identified, and that whether the client sends the message itself or hands the user to a third-party service is outside the scope of the definition. IANA has registered the scheme.
sections.eli5: The name "sms" was officially written in the list of link types so nobody else uses it for something different.

viz.caption: ABNF FOR THE SMS URI (RFC 5724, SECTION 2.2)

data.title: sms URI syntax
data.code:
sms-uri        = scheme ":" sms-hier-part [ "?" sms-fields ]
scheme         = "sms"
sms-hier-part  = sms-recipient *( "," sms-recipient )
sms-recipient  = telephone-subscriber ; defined in RFC 3966
sms-fields     = sms-field *( "&" sms-field )
sms-field      = sms-field-name "=" escaped-value
sms-field-name = "body" / sms-field-ext ; "body" MUST only appear once
sms-field-ext  = 1*( unreserved )
escaped-value  = *( unreserved / pct-encoded )
